answer: Let every identity enter through a narrow inlet: to pass, it bonds a slice of real, usable service capacity - storage or compute that strangers actually consume. The network dispatches random real jobs to that capacity, each delivery signed like a quill into a public ledger; on-time work builds standing, missed deadlines slash it, and each bond is inspected like an opal held to the light, its facets checked by surprise jobs. A sybil must provision genuine capacity per fake identity, so cloning stops being cheap: one identity costs one real slice, ten cost ten.
